full_judgment: 6. The High Court Division held that it is a settled principle of law that the appellate Court below being final Court of fact will have to discuss and reassess the evidence of record independently while either reversing of affirming the finding of the trial Court. In a case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate Court to reassess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent findings. In the instant case, the specific findings of the trial Court have not been reversed by the power appellate Court exercising its appellate jurisdiction under Order XLI, Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
